Subject: SLO fanout, regional throughput & data jurisdiction — post-discovery next steps

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed list of next steps so we can size an initial pilot: 

Summary of what we heard from FinServCo:
- Target latency: 95th percentile <= 120ms for short-chat flows (<=128 tokens) in US and EU; APAC tolerance is relaxed to 250ms for now.
- Throughput: sustained 300 QPS for classification/rerank workload, occasional spikes to 1,200 QPS with burst policy.
- Concurrency: per-customer concurrency cap required at 250 concurrent streams.
- Streaming: customer needs server-side streaming for partial results to render as they arrive; max chunk latency budget 40ms.
- Data residency: PII must remain in customer-managed VPC in EU region for EU tenants; US tenants are fine in Redwood-hosted US regions but logs must be redacted.

Open clarifying questions for our infra team (cc'd):
1) Do the 120ms and 250ms targets assume cold or warm KV-cache? (Aditya)
2) Can we provision dedicated burst capacity for FinServCo's expected 1,200 QPS spikes, or recommend a multi-tier fallback? (Neha)
3) What telemetry will satisfy FinServCo's compliance team for data-residency proof?

Proposed next steps:
- Aditya to provide a short technical note on expected p95 with warm cache + recommended batching config (by Wed).
- Neha to draft capacity/replica plan with canary rollout and fallback to smaller-quantized model variants (by Thu).
- We'll share a short Drive folder with logs & test artifacts and a HubSpot activity for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-slo-fanout-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal sketch)

Thanks — happy to hop on a calibration call if you'd prefer to walk through details.

Best,
Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful. A couple quick notes/questions from our side: 

- The 120ms p95 target is for our customer-facing chat UI where latency is highly visible. We do have a small portion of traffic that requires longer context (up to 512 tokens) — will that materially change the p95 expectation?
- For APAC, the 250ms is an upper bound — lower is better, but we understand routing constraints.
- Regarding data residency: the EU tenants need both model inference to run inside our EU VPC and logs never to leave the VPC. We can provide a read-only S3 bucket inside our VPC for artifacts — is Redwood able to run within customer VPCs for inference?

Also looping infra because they will want to see the proposal PDF and understand the burst model.

On Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:11:00 +0000, Megan Ortiz <m.ortiz@finserv.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful. A couple quick notes/questions from our side:
> - The 120ms p95 target is for our customer-facing chat UI where latency is highly visible. We do have a small portion of traffic that requires longer context (up to 512 tokens) — will that materially change the p95 expectation?
> - For APAC, the 250ms is an upper bound — lower is better, but we understand routing constraints.
> - Regarding data residency: the EU tenants need both model inference to run inside our EU VPC and logs never to leave the VPC. We can provide a read-only S3 bucket inside our VPC for artifacts — is Redwood able to run within customer VPCs for inference?

Hi Megan — quick technical answers: 

1) Short vs long context: p95 will shift non-linearly with context length. For our baseline family (decoder-only, causal models): expect roughly +40–80ms p95 going from 128→512 tokens at similar load/sequence distribution. That assumes warm KV cache and steady batching. If you need 512 often, we should consider a higher-memory instance type and larger KV shard.

2) Streaming/chunk latency: we can sustain chunk delivery within the 40ms budget with continuous batching disabled for streaming routes (we favour low-latency fast-paths). The trade-off is higher per-token cost. We can model that in the pilot.

3) Concurrency and burst plan: we can offer a reserved burst pool that the tenant can draw from (Dedicated capacity) plus a soft fallback to a quantized-but-compatible variant when Dedicated is exhausted. For 1,200 spike QPS with 250 concurrency cap, I'd recommend an initial Dedicated reservation sized at 500 QPS with autoscale headroom to 1,200 during business hours. Neha will propose autoscale thresholds.

4) VPC/Private deployment: Yes — Redwood Private supports running the inference runtime inside a customer-managed VPC (we've done this with two financial customers). For your EU requirement where logs cannot leave the VPC, we can deploy the inference service inside your VPC and integrate with your KMS; logs can be written to customer-managed storage only. We'll need a lightweight agent and an onboarding window to validate compliance.

I'll attach a short sketch of expected p95 numbers for 128/256/512 tokens with warm cache under the throughput envelope you gave — see attached (finserv-demo-logs-sample.tar.gz).

Let us know if you want us to size a dedicated pilot that runs within your VPC for a 2-week validation window.

Cheers,
Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — great alignment. Quick summary and concrete next steps so everyone has the same expectations: 

Decisions so far:
- Pilot scope: 2-week pilot per-tenant using Redwood Private within FinServCo EU VPC for EU tenants and Redwood-hosted US region for US tenants (logs written only to customer storage for EU).
- SLO targets: US/EU p95 target 120ms for <=128 tokens (512-support tracked separately); APAC p95 target 250ms.
- Throughput: Reserved capacity 500 QPS with autoscale headroom to 1,200 QPS for spikes; per-customer concurrency capped at 250.
- Streaming: Enable server-side streaming route with per-chunk budget 40ms; we'll benchmark cost delta during pilot.

Action items: 
- Aditya: Finalize the short p95+throughput note and the config snippet for warm-cache + batching (ETA: Wed 2027-03-24).
- Neha: Draft Dedicated reservation + autoscale thresholds, and the canary rollout plan (ETA: Thu 2027-03-25).
- Jasmine: Create the Drive folder (link below), add the proposal PDF and the pilot runbook, and create HubSpot activity & draft contract language for Private deployment (ETA: Fri 2027-03-19).

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cFinServ-NextSteps
HubSpot deal: DEAL-7423 (I'll add notes and the mutual action plan).

If FinServ infra wants a technical sync, Aditya and Neha are available Thursday/Friday mornings PST — Megan, please propose a 30-min slot if you'd like that before we lock the pilot.
